services.name: Blue Angels Practice and Dolphin Cruise
services.desc: Adults $55.00: Children 5-12: $45.00 Children 4 and under $30.00 About This is a 3 Hour Dolphin Cruise and Blue Angels Practice Tour on Pensacola Bay. Cruise is on our 42' powerboat tritoon passenger vessel, the Jolly Dolphin. We cover a 20 mile round trip, watching for dolphins, and other marine life, while passing by iconic Pensacola Beach landmarks, such as Fort Pickens, the Pensacola Naval Air Station, and the Pensacola Lighthouse. Our cruise stops at Sand Island, a 40 ft sand dune island, where you can view the Blues up close and personal. This island is across from the Pensacola Angels & Dolphins, the ultimate cruise! Up to 28 guests or 40 guests

services.desc: > Sunset time is the main event of the day on Pensacola Beach...and one of best places to watch it happen is from the deck of a sailboat! > The waters of Pensacola Bay and Santa Rosa Sound are renowned for sailing and cruising, with steady afternoon sea-breezes, plenty of depth and easy anchorages. > On the Jolly Mon, our custom 27' American Mariner sailboat, you will experience a sailing adventure to remember. Sailing is a unique experience that is relaxing and exciting at the same time. > Sailing with Come sail into the sunset with us!

services.desc: This cruise takes place on one of our six passenger boats bookable has a semi private ticketed tour or a private tour for up to 6 guests. If booking tickets, please note, we require a minimum of four passengers to operate the cruise. If we do not have at least four guests book, we will contact you and give you the option to reschedule or receive a refund. From the end of March through October, the U.S. Navy’s Flight Demonstration Squadron, the world famous Blue Angels, practice in the skies of their home base of Pensacola. The practices are typically scheduled mornings at 10:30 a.m., Tuesdays Private Dolphin Cruise and Blue Angels Practice Viewing with Island Stop!

On this cruise, we will have time to explore the waters of Pensacola Bay in search of dolphins and other wildlife, in addition to a stop for snorkeling. Depending on where we find the dolphins, you can opt to spend more time in the water, or just cruising around. Trip includes snorkel gear, instruction, and bottled Fun dolphin cruise with a snorkel stop, your private adventure!

services.name: 4 Hour Jolly Mon Blue Angels Practice Sail (up to 6 guests)
services.desc: Watch the Blue Angels from the comfort of the S/V Jolly Mon, offering a special perspective of the US Navy's flight demonstration team during their weekly scheduled practices. These cruises are available most Tuesdays and Wednesdays late March through October per the Blues official practice schedule. On this cruise, we sail or motorsail towards the Naval Air Station, the home of the Blue Angels, and their takeoff location for the practices. The Blues are scheduled to practice at 10:30 a.m. Guests will be able to enjoy the practice from the water, up close and personal! The Angels often fly Enjoy a unique view of the Blue Angels soaring above the deck of our sailboat!

services.name: 4 Hour Jolly Mon Sailing Adventure (up to 6 guests)
services.desc: Climb aboard the Jolly Mon, our 27' sailboat, for a 4 hour sailing adventure with optional swim or snorkel stop! This extended sailing excursion allows plenty of time to cover a lot of water, cruising around Pensacola Bay, Santa Rosa Sound, and/or the Pensacola Pass (entrance to the Gulf of Mexico). Route will depend on conditions. During this cruise we will sail along the beautiful landscape of the National Seashore, taking in the sights and sounds of the open water. Sit back and relax, or take the helm to experience the real joy of sailing! Enjoy the wind in your hair while you look out for Sail away on the Bay! Plenty of time to get a real feel for sailing, and cover lots of water!

faq.a: We sail in the protected waters of Santa Rosa Sound and Pensacola Bay, where conditions are quite favorable for boating. Seasickness is highly unlikely to occur while sailing, as it is generally a much smoother ride than you get on a powerboat. The sails stabilize the boat and keep it from rolling and pitching. Also there are no noxious engine fumes to contend with, which often contributes to the problem. To date, none of our passengers have experienced seasickness on our vessels.
